name: Todoist
summary: Task manager for individuals and small teams: quick capture, due dates and projects across devices. A to-do app, not a project suite with timelines or dependencies.
best_for: individuals and small teams who want a fast, elegant task manager that gets out of the way
skip_if: you need full project management with timelines, workloads and dependencies — this is a to-do app, not a PM suite
honest_knock: The free plan's 5-project cap, and reminders that fire only at the moment a task comes due, push most serious users to Pro quickly — but Pro is genuinely cheap. In our test on 20 October 2026 the sixth project was not created: the attempt opened a 7-day Pro trial offer instead. It's a personal/team task manager, not a full project platform, so don't expect Gantt-level PM.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month billed annually ($60/yr) or $7 billed monthly
pricing.notes: (re-verified 25 September 2026 on todoist.com/pricing, currency set to USD, both billing toggles) Free Beginner plan: 5 personal projects, 3 filter views, 5 MB uploads, one week of activity history and one automatic reminder per task. Pro $5 a month billed annually ($60 a year) or $7 billed monthly, with 300 personal projects, custom reminders, calendar layout, task duration, deadlines and full history. Business $8 per user a month billed annually ($96 a year) or $10 monthly, plus local tax, adding a shared team workspace with 500 team projects and up to 1,000 members and guests.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on a new free Beginner account: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser. We built one project with tasks, a sub-task, a section, a priority and a date typed in plain words, then created projects until the free plan's limit appeared.
findings: A new account started at '0 projects' with a 'Free' label; the Inbox does not count as a project.
Typing 'Review today' was recognised while typing: Todoist highlighted 'today', removed it from the task name and saved a task called 'Review' due Today, and the Today view counted 1.
A sub-task added through the task details sat indented under its parent, which then showed a '0/1' counter. A section 'Later' came from the project menu with its own Add task.
A completed task disappeared from the list and came back struck through under Display > Completed tasks; the project counter showed 4 open tasks.
From the fourth project the sidebar showed 'USED: 4/5', then 'USED: 5/5'.

The sixth project was not created. The attempt went straight to 'Try Pro for free': yearly billing at €5/month ('SAVE €24'), 'Due today (7 days free) €0' and 'Due 27 Oct 2026 €60/year', for 300 projects and 150 filter views. The projects page then said '5 projects' with 'Need more projects? ... Upgrade'.
The 'Try Pro for free' window also appeared once, unasked, while creating the very first project.
